content.title: Warriors Forward Jimmy Butler III to Miss Remainder of 2025-26 Season | Golden State Warriors
content.text: Jimmy Butler III was having a night against his former team, with 17 points in 21 minutes en route to beating them for the first time since his departure nearly a year ago. However, with 7:41 remaining in the third quarter, all of that momentum came to a screeching halt as Butler suffered a season-ending ACL injury. He and the Warriors were playing their best basketball of the season, amidst their longest winning streak (4 games) and improving to six games over .500 (25-19). Butler had scored in double figures in 18 straight games, including 15-or-more points in 17 of those games. “Most of all, just disappointed for Jimmy,” Head Coach Steve Kerr said. “He was having a great year. I felt like the last couple of weeks, he was really at the top of his game. It hurts for sure.”Since he joined the team on Feb. 6, 2025, the Warriors have a 46-22 record with Butler on the court and advanced to the second round of the playoffs for the first time since 2023. Without him over that span, they are just 2-7. “Tough 24 hours here for our group, our organization, most especially crushed for Jimmy, who was having a great year and obviously it’s over now,” General Manager Mike Dunleavy said. “We’re disappointed as a team, as an organization, most especially though, individually for Jimmy, who’s meant so much to this organization since he got here. It’s hard to believe he hasn’t even been here a year and he’s fit in so well. You know you hate it for him, but the beat goes on, we gotta keep going and I think our team’s playing really well.”Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 11:33Remaining Time 11:33Warriors Talk: Mike Dunleavy on Jimmy Butler's Injury, Previews Trade Deadline – 01/20/2026Dunleavy remains hopeful that Butler will make a full recovery and return to be a similar two-way force at some point next season. Butler is currently 36 years old and the second-oldest player in the last 20 NBA seasons to suffer an ACL tear. That said, with the advancements of modern medicine, there have been numerous success stories of players returning to form after injuries previously viewed as career-ending or altering. The most recent and relevant example within the team is De’Anthony Melton’s return after an ACL tear last season. Melton is averaging 14.3 points per game on a 62.2 true shooting percentage over his last eight games and has eclipsed 20 points three times over that span, which accounts for half of his six highest-scoring games since 2023. “What I envision for him [Butler] is giving us a boost next year, the same way he did last year when he arrived,” Dunleavy said. “So, at some point during the season, he's returning and being the player he's been. At his age, what he's doing this year, to have the year he's had is impressive. I think he's got a style of game that can play for a long time with his skill, his physicality and his mind for the game. My vision for him is him returning at some point between now and this time next year.” In the meantime, it’s clear to Dunleavy, Kerr and the leaders of the organization that the Warriors are worse off without their second-best player and that it will take a collective effort to fill that void. That said, the Warriors do believe they are in a better position, from a roster-construction standpoint, to fare without Butler than before they acquired him, thanks to their veteran offseason additions and their recent draft successes. “The difference from last year to this year, to me, is De’Anthony Melton and Al Horford,” Kerr said. “Not to mention Quinten Post for a full year. At this stage last year, before we traded for Jimmy, it didn't feel like we had enough to really compete. I think we have enough to compete. I think Al and Melt have given us a different dynamic. I think a lot of our young players, you know, Quinten, Will Richard, those guys are ready to contribute, they have contributed. We've got depth.”In their first game since the injury, Kerr went deep into his bench, re-inserting Jonathan Kuminga into the rotation after 16 straight DNP’s. And Kuminga, who has been lauded for being a constant professional and always staying ready, delivered when given his opportunity, scoring 20 points on 7-for-10 shooting in 21 minutes. “He’s [Kuminga] been here working every single day, then you allow yourself the opportunity to go out and have that game because you've prepared for it,” Draymond Green said. “He’s prepared for whatever came next and it showed tonight and it’ll continue to show because he’ll continue to prepare and he is who he is as a person.”“He's [Kuminga] available every night,” Dunleavy added. “I think there's a path and a way for him to help us win games. He knows what that is. If he can do those things, there's no doubt I think he can help us.”Kerr has highlighted the struggles of Kuminga and Butler lineup combinations due to their overlapping play styles — they share similar strengths and weaknesses, particularly on the offensive end, typically operating in the same spots. But with Butler unable to play, some of those similarities can help the team in their transition, as they learn to play without the six-time All-Star, who finished top-20 in fan voting this year. “Jimmy is who Jimmy is for a reason,” Green said. “So to think that A it’s one person going to fix it, or B we’re going to fix it in one day, it’s not realistic. That would be kind of lessening the value of what Jimmy brings and we know what that value is.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 4:02Remaining Time 4:02Postgame Warriors Talk: Draymond Green - 01/20/2026Dunleavy is taking the next few weeks to evaluate the team in its new state, having to completely shift his trade deadline approach after the Butler news. “As far as it goes with the deadline coming up, I think we'll take the next couple of weeks to assess this team a little bit more,” Dunleavy said. “I felt pretty good with where we're at heading into last night's game in terms of what we need to do. I thought our team was playing really well, heading in the right direction, obviously things have changed, so I want to take a couple of weeks here to watch these games and see our team and what we can do better.”He is open to trading draft picks to improve the roster, but when looking at his premium draft capital, which would likely be conveyed when franchise player Stephen Curry is retired, he’s going to have to get a younger player back who is still going to be highly impactful for the franchise in that draft year. The NBA trade deadline is on Feb. 5 and the Warriors have six games between now and then. Those six games and the moves made between them will go a long way in dictating the direction of this season and in some ways shape the team’s outlook moving forward into next year. Amidst all the unknown, the organization remains confident in its leadership at General Manager, Head Coach and veterans Curry and Green. “I believe we can figure it out,” Green said. “What that means for us long term? I don't know. If I had all the answers right now, I would gladly give them to you, but I just don't.”
